extracted.intended_audience: researchers/engineers and teams preparing proposals to DARPA's World Modelers program (technology developers for national-security modeling)
extracted.subtask_description: Specifications and expected capabilities for technologies to be developed under DARPA's World Modelers program: integrated modeling systems that combine qualitative causal analysis, quantitative models, and data to support timely, actionable national-security analyses at subnational scales over a 1–5 year horizon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of qualitative causal analyses with quantitative models and data
rubrics_metrics.description: The program aims to develop technology that integrates qualitative causal analyses with quantitative models and relevant data to provide a comprehensive understanding of complicated, dynamic national security questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technologies should combine causal (qualitative) reasoning and mechanistic/statistical (quantitative) models along with pertinent data sources so that analyses are comprehensive rather than purely quantitative or purely narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability / multi-model connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal is to develop approaches that can accommodate and integrate dozens of contributing models connected by thousands of pathways—orders of magnitude beyond what is possible today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architectures must support many heterogeneous models and a very large number of inter-model interactions/pathways, far exceeding current capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and actionability
rubrics_metrics.description: World Modelers analyses are intended to be timely enough to recommend specific actions that could avert crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses must deliver results quickly enough to inform decisions and recommend concrete actions that could prevent or mitigate crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid, clearly parameterized quantitative projections
rubrics_metrics.description: The program seeks to develop technologies that will provide clearly parameterized, quantitative projections within weeks or even hours of processing, compared to the months or years it takes today to understand considerably simpler systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projections should be explicit about parameters and uncertainty, and be computable on timelines of hours to weeks rather than months/years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability across multiple use cases and program phases
rubrics_metrics.description: World Modelers technologies will be applied to increasingly varied use cases as they mature through the phases of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions should generalize or be adaptable so they can be applied to different problem domains and evolve across program phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subnational spatial focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions for analysis will typically be framed at subnational scales ... This subnational focus reflects the changing nature of conflict and security, which, increasingly, plays out in cities and districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should be capable of resolving and reasoning at subnational granularity (e.g., city, district) rather than only at national or global scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1–5 year temporal horizon (with multi-scale awareness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions ... look one to five years into the future, although the factors that influence outcomes of interest might operate on larger spatial and temporal scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should primarily target a 1–5 year forecasting horizon while retaining the ability to represent influences that act on broader/longer scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to represent multi-scale factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The factors that influence outcomes of interest might operate on larger spatial and temporal scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must reconcile and represent interactions across scales (e.g., local effects influenced by regional or global processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: First use-case requirement: food insecurity from interacting factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The first use case of World Modelers is food insecurity resulting from the interactions of multiple factors, including climate, water availability, soil viability, market instability, and physical security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial demonstrations should address food insecurity as a complex, multi-factor problem integrating environmental, economic, and security-related submodels and data streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver comprehensive understanding of dynamic national-security questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a comprehensive understanding of complicated, dynamic national security questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond producing forecasts, systems should enable an understanding of causal mechanisms, interactions, and intervention points relevant to national-security decision-making.
